criteria: knowledge and understanding of course content
application of business case studies and contemporary business issues
answer:
Executive summary
Online orders at Tidewater Outfitters have grown every year since 2022 while its store sales have fallen. This report recommends redesigning the warehouse for single online orders, turning two stores into click-and-collect points, and renegotiating the store leases on shorter terms as they expire.

Findings
Online orders per week rose from about 250 in 2022 to about 700 in 2025. The warehouse was designed to send bulk stock to six stores, so it is slow at picking single online orders, and delivery times have slipped. All six store leases expire within the next two years.

Recommendations
Tidewater should redesign its warehouse layout for single-order picking. This would shorten delivery times for the customers who are now buying online.
The business should also keep its six stores but convert two of them into click-and-collect points. This keeps the owners' stores open while making them part of the online sale.
Finally, the business should renegotiate its leases for shorter terms as each one expires.

Conclusion
By changing how the warehouse works and giving the stores a role in online sales, Tidewater can respond to where its customers are buying without closing a store.

review.summary: This reads as a business report. It has headings, it separates what was found from what is recommended, and it keeps the owners' six stores in view. The findings are specific, and the warehouse recommendation follows directly from them. The other two recommendations are stated rather than reasoned, and none of the three goes back to the growth in online orders to show why it is the right size of response.

rubric.name: knowledge and understanding of course content
rubric.descriptor: Rewards accurate course content, used to answer the question rather than to display it.

rubric.name: application of business case studies and contemporary business issues
rubric.descriptor: Rewards a business used as evidence for the argument, not described alongside it.

rubric.name: business terminology and concepts
rubric.descriptor: Rewards terminology that carries the reasoning rather than decorating it.

rubric.name: sustained, logical and cohesive response
rubric.descriptor: Rewards one judgement held from the first paragraph to the last.

sentences.text: The response is organised under report headings.

issues.head: It reads as a report
issues.why: Headings separate what you found from what you recommend, and the executive summary gives the whole answer in two sentences. A reader could act on this without reading every line.

sentences.text: The warehouse was designed to send bulk stock to six stores, so it is slow at picking single online orders, and delivery times have slipped.

issues.head: The operations problem is identified precisely
issues.why: You say why the warehouse struggles, not just that it does: it was designed to send bulk stock to stores, and picking single online orders is a different job. That is the cause the rest of the report can build on.

sentences.text: Finally, the business should renegotiate its leases for shorter terms as each one expires.

issues.head: This recommendation is stated but not justified
issues.why: You recommend shorter leases but do not say how they help the business respond to online buying. Say what shorter terms would let the owners do, and use your own finding that every lease ends within two years to show why now is the time.

sentences.text: This keeps the owners' stores open while making them part of the online sale.

issues.head: The owners' wish is kept, but only two stores are given a role
issues.why: Converting two stores keeps all six open, which is what the owners want. The report never says what the other four are for while store sales keep falling, and that is the question the owners will ask first.

sentences.text: None of the recommendations draws on the order figures.

issues.head: The recommendations do not return to your own figures
issues.why: Your findings give online orders rising from about 250 to about 700 a week, and no recommendation uses that growth to show why it is the right response or how large it needs to be.
